---
title: Rewrite levels
icon: SlidersHorizontal
description: Choose how far Wakaru rewrites your code.
---

Wakaru uses `standard` by default. Change the level when you want to stay
closer to the input's behavior or try stronger recovery.

## Choosing a level

| Level | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| `minimal` | You are auditing, debugging, or trying to run the recovered code. Behavioral fidelity comes first |
| `standard` | You want readable code with modern syntax. This is the default |
| `aggressive` | You want to try further recovery and can accept changes to edge-case behavior |

```bash
npx wakaru input.js --level minimal
npx wakaru input.js                     # standard is the default
npx wakaru input.js --level aggressive
```

## See the difference

Consider a function that reads a user's name or falls back to `"Anonymous"`:

```js title="Input"
function displayName(user) {
    return user.name != null ? user.name : "Anonymous";
}
```

With `minimal`, Wakaru keeps the two property reads:

```js title="minimal"
function displayName(user) {
    if (user.name != null) {
        return user.name;
    }
    return "Anonymous";
}
```

With `standard`, it recovers nullish coalescing:

```js title="standard"
function displayName(user) {
    return user.name ?? "Anonymous";
}
```

For a plain object such as `{ name: "Ada" }`, both return `"Ada"`.
The difference matters when `name` is a getter: the first version reads it
twice when the value is present, while the second reads it once. A getter
can have side effects or return a different value on each read.

Try each version separately with this `user`:

```js
let reads = 0;
const user = {
    get name() {
        reads += 1;
        return reads === 1 ? "Ada" : "Grace";
    }
};

console.log(displayName(user)); // minimal: "Grace", standard: "Ada"
```

In `minimal`, the condition reads `"Ada"`, then the return reads `"Grace"`.
In `standard`, `??` reads `"Ada"` once and returns it.

`minimal` preserves that behavior. `standard` favors the familiar `??` form,
assuming the property is stable and reading it has no side effects.
`aggressive` produces the same result as `standard` in this example. A higher
level does not always change the output.

You can compare levels on your own code in the [playground](/guides/playground).
The full [rewrite assumptions](https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/blob/main/docs/rewrite-assumptions.md)
explain the recovery choices each level permits.

## Dead code

Dead-code removal is a separate choice. By default, Wakaru removes only the
dead code its own transforms create. Dead code that already existed in the
input stays. Opt into a full reachability sweep with:

```bash
npx wakaru input.js --dce
```
